name: Mysuru Palace
history: Seat of the Wadiyar dynasty; the present Indo-Saracenic palace was completed in 1912 after the earlier wooden palace burned down. It is lit by nearly 100,000 bulbs on Sundays and during Dasara.
photoTip: Visit on a Sunday evening for the stunning illumination.

name: Chamundi Hills
history: Hilltop temple of Goddess Chamundeshwari overlooking Mysuru, with the large Nandi monolith on the way up the 1,000-step path.
photoTip: City panorama from the hill top at sunset.

name: Srirangapatna Fort & Ranganathaswamy
history: Island fortress on the Kaveri — capital of Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan. The Ranganathaswamy temple here is one of the most important Vaishnava pilgrimage sites in the South.
photoTip: Kaveri riverfront near Gosai Ghat at dawn.

name: Hampi – Virupaksha Temple & Hampi Bazaar
history: UNESCO World Heritage capital of the Vijayanagara Empire (14th–16th c.); Virupaksha is still a living, active temple.
photoTip: Hampi Bazaar at early morning light — ruins with no crowds.

name: Hampi – Vittala Temple & Stone Chariot
history: Famed for its musical pillars and the iconic stone chariot — a showpiece of Vijayanagara architecture.
photoTip: Soft golden light after 4 pm; drone use is restricted.

name: Matanga Hill Sunrise
history: Highest point near the ruins with 360° panoramic views over boulders and the Tungabhadra river.
photoTip: Climb before sunrise with a torch; avoid solitary night climbs.

name: Badami Cave Temples
history: Rock-cut Chalukya caves of the 6th century above the Agastya lake in red sandstone.
photoTip: Sandstone glows orange-red in late afternoon.

name: Pattadakal Group of Monuments
history: UNESCO World Heritage site where Chalukyan north and south Indian temple styles uniquely converge.
photoTip: Golden hour light on the Virupaksha temple.

name: Aihole – Cradle of Indian Architecture
history: Over 125 temples from the 4th–8th centuries, the earliest Hindu, Jain, and Buddhist stone temples in the Deccan.
photoTip: Durga temple and Lad Khan temple at sunrise.

name: Chennakeshava Temple, Belur
history: Hoysala gem consecrated in 1117 CE; its Shilabalikas (bracket figures) are among the finest medieval sculpture in India.
photoTip: Dress modestly; photography rules apply inside the sanctum.

name: Hoysaleswara Temple, Halebidu
history: 12th-century twin-shrine Hoysala temple with a 40-m long frieze showing elephants, lions, scrolling foliage, epics, and gods.
photoTip: Low-angle morning light reveals the carved friezes.

name: Shravanabelagola
history: The 17.7-m monolithic Gommateshwara statue (981 CE) atop Vindhyagiri hill — the tallest freestanding statue in India at its creation.
photoTip: Climb early morning; bare feet required on the rock steps.

name: Gokarna – Om Beach
history: Om-shaped beach near Gokarna town; flanked by the Mahabaleshwar temple. Attracts backpackers and pilgrims alike.
photoTip: Sunset from the cliff viewpoints; swim only in calm season.

name: Udupi Sri Krishna Matha
history: 8th-century Krishna temple founded by Madhvacharya; the birthplace of Udupi cuisine — the Brahmin cook tradition of the South.
photoTip: Rath Street at dusk; free Anna Prasad (community lunch) daily.

name: Murudeshwar Temple & Shiva Statue
history: Seaside Shiva temple with a 123-ft Shiva statue visible from the Konkan railway — one of the tallest in the world.
photoTip: Shiva statue silhouetted against the sunset sky from the beach.

name: St. Mary's Islands
history: Hexagonal basalt rock formations created by volcanic activity 88 million years ago; Vasco da Gama planted a cross here in 1498.
photoTip: Reach by boat from Malpe; the basalt columns photograph best at low tide.

name: Jog Falls
history: The Sharavathi river plunges 253 m in four distinct falls — Raja, Rani, Rocket, and Roarer. Best visited just after the monsoon.
photoTip: Viewpoint on the Shimoga side; stay behind railings — currents are fatal.

name: Agumbe Rainforest
history: Called the 'Cherrapunji of South India', Agumbe gets 7,000 mm of rain. It is the last stronghold of the king cobra and the setting for Malgudi Days.
photoTip: Sunset Point at the ghat top; leech socks essential in monsoon.

name: Abbey Falls, Coorg
history: 60-ft twin falls surrounded by coffee and spice plantations; the estate walk through the plantation is equally memorable.
photoTip: Misty morning after monsoon rain — waterfall at full power.

name: Coorg Coffee Plantation Trail
history: Coorg (Kodagu) produces about 30% of India's coffee. Arabica and Robusta estates offer guided walks through shade-grown coffee under silver oaks and pepper vines.
photoTip: Coffee blossom season (Feb–Mar) — jasmine-scented white flowers cover the estate.

name: Raja's Seat, Madikeri
history: Garden viewpoint where the Kodagu (Coorg) kings once watched sunsets over the Western Ghats valley.
photoTip: Sunset and misty mornings in winter months.

name: Talacauvery – Source of Kaveri
history: Sacred source of the Kaveri river in the Western Ghats. The tank here is believed to be fed by an underground spring and overflows on Tula Sankramana day each year.
photoTip: Brahmagiri hill trek for valley views; peak blooms July–August.

name: Mullayanagiri Peak
history: Karnataka's highest peak at 1,930 m in the Baba Budan Giri range; reached by a short but steep stair-climb from the car park.
photoTip: Sunrise above the cloud sea; start the drive before 4 am.

name: Chikkamagaluru Coffee Hills
history: First coffee in India was planted here by Baba Budan in the 17th century. The hills now host hundreds of estates with homestay options inside working plantations.
photoTip: Golden hour across the estate canopy; mist lingers till 9 am.

name: Kabini Backwaters & Safari
history: Kabini reservoir on the edge of Nagarhole National Park — one of the best places in India to spot elephants, leopards, and tigers in open deciduous forest.
photoTip: Dawn and dusk Jeep safaris; boat safari for birdwatching.

name: Dandeli Wildlife Sanctuary
history: Dense teak forest on the Kali river — home to black panthers, gaur, and over 300 bird species. Offers river rafting and bamboo rafting.
photoTip: River-side bird hides in the morning; crested serpent eagle is common.

name: Nagarhole National Park
history: Part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve; supports about 30 tigers and over 5,000 elephants. Elephant corridors connect to Bandipur and Mudumalai.
photoTip: Elephant herds in open grasslands at dusk.

name: Bandipur Tiger Reserve
history: One of India's premier Project Tiger reserves; contiguous with Nagarhole, Mudumalai, and Wayanad creating the largest protected forest in South India.
photoTip: Gaur (Indian bison) very visible; book a government bus safari for quieter viewing.

name: Nandi Hills
history: Hill fortress 60 km from Bengaluru; summer retreat of Tipu Sultan. The Bhoga Nandeeshwara temple at the base has temples from three dynasties.
photoTip: Weekday sunrise — far fewer crowds than weekends.

name: Bidar Fort & Bahmani Tombs
history: 15th-century Bahmani sultanate fort with the Rangin Mahal — one of the finest examples of Persian-Deccani architecture with mother-of-pearl inlay.
photoTip: Rangin Mahal tilework in early morning light.

name: Gulbarga Fort & Jama Masjid
history: The Jama Masjid (1367) here is the only mosque in India with a fully covered courtyard — modelled on the Great Mosque of Córdoba, Spain.
photoTip: The mosque's arched interior arcade is unique in India.

name: Chitradurga Fort
history: Built across seven concentric layers of granite hill — Onake Obavva, the lone woman warrior, defended it using a pestle. The fort spans 1,500 acres.
photoTip: Panorama from the topmost bastion; sunrise and sunset equally dramatic.

name: Bisle Reserve Forest Trek, Sakleshpur
history: Dense shola forest in the Western Ghats with views of three states on a clear day. Elephants and leopards roam freely; guide is mandatory.
photoTip: Morning mist rolls in from the valley — the ghats at their most ethereal.

name: Kudremukh National Park
history: Kudremukh ('horse face' in Kannada) is the source of the Bhadra river. The peak (1,894 m) sits inside a national park; trekking requires a Forest Dept permit.
photoTip: The rolling shola grasslands — rare montane ecosystem unique to the Western Ghats.

name: Yana Caves & Rock Formations
history: Yana's 120-m Bhairaveshwara Shikhara and 90-m Mohini Shikhara are two massive free-standing crystalline limestone rocks in the middle of a dense tropical forest.
photoTip: The rocks appear to pierce the jungle canopy — the 1-km forest walk to them is the shot.

name: Belum Caves – Kurnool (near border)
history: Belum Caves — second-longest natural cave system in the Indian subcontinent at 3.5 km. Jain and Buddhist monks used to meditate here; the 'Pataalaganga' underground stream is a highlight.
photoTip: The stalactites and stalagmites in 'Simhachalam' chamber are best photographed with a tripod.

name: Mysuru Dasara Festival
history: Karnataka's state festival — 10-day celebration culminating in the Jamboo Savari elephant procession on Vijayadashami. Mysuru has celebrated Dasara for 400+ years.
photoTip: The illuminated palace on Vijayadashami night — use a tripod from Mysuru Zoo side.

name: Yakshagana Performance, Udupi
history: Yakshagana is a 300-year-old composite dance-drama of the Tulu Nadu coast — combining elaborate head-dress, face paint, and all-night storytelling from the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
photoTip: The elaborate headdress ('mundasu') and make-up are the shot — ask for permission before close-ups.

name: Lambani Tribal Embroidery Village, Sandur
history: Lambani (Banjara) women practice a distinctive mirror-work embroidery — each piece takes weeks and tells stories in geometric patterns. Sandur's habitations preserve this living art.
photoTip: The colourful everyday dress against the ochre village walls is striking portraiture.

name: Keshava Temple, Somnathpur
history: One of the best-preserved Hoysala triple temples (1268 CE) with 180-ft of carved friezes visible from outside. The mandapa's lathe-turned pillars are masterworks.
photoTip: Starfish plan shape best seen from the east entrance gate.

name: Tungabhadra Dam & Hampi Backwaters
history: The 1953 dam created the Tungabhadra reservoir that forms Hampi's backwater landscape. The garden and evening musical fountain are popular with families.
photoTip: Sunset over the reservoir with the Hampi hills as backdrop.

name: Dharmasthala Temple & Museum
history: A 700-year-old Shiva temple managed by the Jain Heggade family — unique for being a Hindu temple where the hereditary administrator is Jain. Free meals for all pilgrims daily.
photoTip: The 39-ft Bahubali statue and the carriage museum adjacent.

name: Maravanthe Beach
history: A narrow strip of beach where NH-66 runs between the Arabian Sea on one side and the Souparnika river on the other — one of the most photogenic road-beach-river compositions in India.
photoTip: Aerial-like shot from the coastal hill to the north; the NH-66 bridge framing.

name: Gokarna – Mahabaleshwar Temple
history: One of the seven muktikshethras of Shiva; the Atmalinga here is believed to be the original Shivalinga that Ravana obtained from Shiva. Important pilgrimage for South Indian Hindus.
photoTip: The main car street (Koti Teertha Street) in the evening puja light.

name: Omkareshwara Temple & Fort, Madikeri
history: An unusual 19th-century temple in Gothic and Islamic style built by Lingarajendra Wadiyar II of Coorg. The fort next door now houses a museum and a cemetery with the royal tombs.
photoTip: The Islamic-Gothic fusion architecture of the temple is architecturally unique.

name: Mangaluru – St. Aloysius Chapel
history: A late 19th-century Jesuit chapel with interior walls and ceiling entirely covered with paintings by Italian artist Antonio Moscheni — the Sistine Chapel of Coastal Karnataka.
photoTip: Interior ceiling paintings require a wide angle and available light.

name: Trikuteshwara Temple, Gadag
history: A complex of Chalukya-era temples (11th–12th c.) whose carved panels are considered the finest examples of Kalyani Chalukyan sculpture — less visited than Hampi but equally detailed.
photoTip: The sardula (lion-faced creature) friezes in afternoon light.

name: Mysuru Silk Weaving Unit, Mysuru
history: KSIC's weaving unit produces Mysore Silk sarees — 3,000 weavers operate Jacquard looms weaving pure silk with real gold zari. The showroom and weaving floor are open to visitors.
photoTip: The weaving floor — rows of looms with silk threads catching the light.

name: Lakkundi Temples
history: A village with 101 monuments including the Brahma Jinalaya (1000 CE) — one of the earliest Jain temples in the Deccan — and intricate Kalyani Chalukya step-wells.
photoTip: The ornate entrance tower (shikhara) of Kashi Vishwanatha temple at golden hour.
